_about: Species conditions used by fishon_engine.species_scoring (engine 2.5.0). Each factor is a condition the species is said to prefer, with the claim and a source. A window that misses a factor loses 'penalty' points from the window's safety-gated score, so a species never scores above the window. The direction of each factor is sourced; the penalty sizes and numeric cut-offs not stated in a source are engine tuning (marked 'threshold_note'). Factors we looked for but could not source, or where sources disagree, are listed under 'left_out' and not scored. Species not listed here (e.g. trevally, john dory, hapuku, groper, barracouta, trout, salmon) are not species-scored. Checked 2026-10-26 NZDT.

factors.claim: Inshore spawning aggregations form once the sea reaches roughly 14.8-16 C; NIWA puts the spring spawning migration at about 16 C.
sources: Parsons et al. 2014, 'Snapper (Chrysophrys auratus): a review of life history and key vulnerabilities in New Zealand', NZ J Marine & Freshwater Research 48(2). https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00288330.2014.892013
NIWA: spring spawning migrations at about 16 C. https://niwa.co.nz/news/will-it-be-fintastic-fishing-year

factors.claim: Snapper fishing is consistently better when the tide is running, particularly on the East Coast.
factors.threshold_note: Slack is taken as within 45 min of high or low (the engine's existing tide rule).
sources: NZ Fishing News / fishing.net.nz, 'How to catch snapper'. https://www.fishing.net.nz/how-to-catch/snapper/

factors.claim: Dawn and dusk is a prime time for snapper, since many fish rely on low light for camouflage, especially in shallow water.
sources: NZ Fishing News / fishing.net.nz, 'How to catch snapper'. https://www.fishing.net.nz/how-to-catch/snapper/

left_out.reason: Fishing lore on the moon is mixed and we found no NZ research showing a moon effect on snapper catch; the generic moon bonus in the window score is unchanged.
Sources say most spots fish better on one tide or the other, but which one is local, so only 'running vs slack' is used.

factors.claim: In the coldest months kingfish go deeper, are less common around the rocks and act sluggishly; once water temps climb to around 16-17 C they become more active and common around the rocks.
sources: Mark Draper, 'Kingfish from the rocks pt 1', NZ Fishing News July 2008, via fishing.net.nz. https://www.fishing.net.nz/fishing-advice/fishing-hints-tips-and-how-to-articles/kingfish-from-the-rocks-pt-1/

Supporting: NIWA yellowtail kingfish growth trials, growth best at 18-26.5 C and falling away below about 15 C (NZ J Marine & Freshwater Research 2014). https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00288330.2014.930050

factors.claim: Daybreak is the best time to fool kingfish in shallow water.
sources: NZ Fishing News / fishing.net.nz, 'Using bite times'. https://www.fishing.net.nz/fishing-advice/fishing-hints-tips-and-how-to-articles/using-bite-times/

left_out.reason: Sources only say some spots fire over a change of tide; nothing general enough to score.

factors.claim: Dawn and dusk are prime times to target kahawai (Clutha River mouth).
sources: Peter Davy, 'Clutha River mouth kahawai', NZ Fishing Magazine, 21 Feb 2026. https://fishingmag.co.nz/south-island/otago-fishing-destinations/clutha-river-mouth-kahawai

left_out.reason: Sources disagree on which tide (incoming vs outgoing) suits river-mouth kahawai; it is local.

Sourced (kahawai are clear-water feeders and move away after rain: fishing.net.nz 'Targeting mainland river mouth kahawai'; fishingmag.co.nz Clutha article) but not modelled: it needs rainfall history and only applies at river mouths.

factors.claim: Gurnard are reluctant to enter the shallows and avoid white water; clean water with low surf is the key to surfcasting success.
factors.threshold_note: The 1.0 m sea cut-off is engine tuning; the sources give no number.
sources: Andy Macleod, 'Land based gurnard fishing', NZ Fishing News April 2018, via fishing.net.nz. https://www.fishing.net.nz/fishing-advice/fishing-hints-tips-and-how-to-articles/land-based-gurnard-fishing/
NZ Fishing News / fishing.net.nz, 'Expert tips to catch gurnard'. https://www.fishing.net.nz/fishing-advice/fishing-hints-tips-and-how-to-articles/expert-tips-to-catch-gurnard/

factors.claim: Surfcasters bag good catches over summer, particularly those that fish the evening change of light.
sources: NZ Fishing News / fishing.net.nz, 'Expert tips to catch gurnard'. https://www.fishing.net.nz/fishing-advice/fishing-hints-tips-and-how-to-articles/expert-tips-to-catch-gurnard/

left_out.reason: Sources disagree by coast (current flowing on the east coast vs slack in west coast harbours).
One source says gurnard don't like warm water but gives no range.

factors.claim: Tarakihi congregate and feed in areas of higher current; the bite turns on as the tide starts to push and dies off at slack.
factors.threshold_note: Slack is taken as within 45 min of high or low.
sources: Sam Boothroyd, 'Chasing sea turkeys: tips and tricks for tarakihi', NZ Fishing News November 2021, via fishing.net.nz. https://www.fishing.net.nz/fishing-advice/fishing-hints-tips-and-how-to-articles/chasing-sea-turkeys-tips-and-tricks-for-tarakihi/

factors.claim: Blue cod are diurnal predators; anglers report they feed at dawn, dusk and occasionally in the day, and appear not to feed at all in the dark.
sources: University of Auckland research on the blue cod lateral line (diurnal predator). https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/items/1229eb18-1dfb-4920-8f94-55966835978a
NZ Fishing News / fishing.net.nz, 'How to catch blue cod from the shore'. https://www.fishing.net.nz/fishing-advice/fishing-hints-tips-and-how-to-articles/how-to-catch-blue-cod-from-the-shore/

left_out.reason: A Fisheries NZ pot survey in the Marlborough Sounds (BCO9701) found no significant tide or time-of-day effect on blue cod catch rates, so tide is deliberately not scored. https://fs.fish.govt.nz/Doc/22461/BCO9701%20Blue%20Cod%20Marlborough%20Sounds%20abundance%20structure%20sex%20ratio.pdf.ashx
An angler source says the dawn and dusk bites can be very intense, but the same Fisheries NZ pot survey found no time-of-day effect; only the dark penalty is used.

not_scored.reason: No NZ source we found gives a usable sea-temperature, tide or light preference (Fisheries NZ FAR 2021/16 and 2025/52 only report the sea temperature during particular seasons, e.g. over 18 C off Cape Runaway in 2025). They are also offshore boat fish, so the shore safety gate does not describe their trips. Seasons stay in species_seasons.json.
